title: digitalis purpurea var. nevadensis
intro: Digitalis purpurea var. nevadensis, commonly known as Western foxglove, is a variety of the Foxglove plant. It is a biennial herb that belongs to the plantain family (Plantaginaceae) and is native to the western United States and Canada. The health benefits of Western foxglove include its potential to treat heart conditions such as atrial fibrillation and congestive heart failure due to its ability to increase the strength of heart muscle contractions. The therapeutic actions of Western foxglove are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including glycosides like digoxin and digitoxin, which have positive inotropic and negative chronotropic effects, and its ability to inhibit the sodium-potassium ATPase pump, thereby slowing heart rate and increasing contractility.
